Thanks for taking this on. We're about to kick the vendor procurement for our on-prem attachment and need a short but thorough reference pack for our network and ops teams:

- Final control plane / data plane topology diagram we should hand to colo/networking (single-page).
- Operator runbook snippets for: tenant provisioning, KV cache failover, and egress proofing.
- Minimal list of required BGP sessions / ACL expectations and expected failover behavior.

Hannah / Li — forwarding the update. Attached: vpc-topology-v2.drawio and operator-runbook-diff.md. Highlights below.

---- forwarded message ----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Li Chen <li.chen@finco.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Sep 2028 09:30:00 +0100

Li — attached are the artifacts. Summary of developer/ops facing changes since the pilot diagram: 

1) Control plane placement: introduced a dedicated control-plane subnet in the customer VPC attached via Direct Connect/colo BGP. This isolates API/control traffic from data plane peerings.

2) Data plane HA: dual leaf attachments per tenant with active/passive KV cache primaries and zookeeper-style leader election at the service layer. The diagram annotates tie-breaker behavior on WAN failover (preferred site stays primary until explicit switchover).

3) Egress proofing: default behavior is to prefer customer-managed NAT for outbound to third-party services; Redwood can provide an egress proxy sidecar for customers that require token-level telemetry. The one-page egress note lists ports and a minimal ACL set.

4) BGP expectations: we propose two sessions — one for control plane (management ASN peer) and one optional for data plane (tenant peer). The runbook includes sample neighbor config and keepalive settings.

Open decision items we called out in the runbook-diff: 
- Whether procurement wants explicit runbook steps for KMS key rotation in the on-prem connector (we left a TODO).
- Confirm retention window for KV cache snapshots (30m vs 2h) and impact on restart recovery.
- Edge vendor (EdgeNexus) needs to confirm jumbo frame support — flagged in diagram.

Attachments: vpc-topology-v2.drawio, operator-runbook-diff.md

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Staff Infrastructure Architect
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Hannah — received, thank you. Quick notes after a cursory review:

- Diagram looks good and the control/data separation is clear. We like the explicit control-plane BGP session.
- Two asks from NOC: please add a short blurb in the runbook on how we verify KV cache consistency after a leader failover (suggested checks and log paths).
- EdgeNexus: can you confirm jumbo frame support and MTU recommendations (we run 9000 in the colo).

Procurement: this is sufficient to move forward; we'll keep the 10/02 deadline but need the small edits above by EOD 09/28 so legal can include the artifacts in the RFP.

Li
